monologue: I wake to a card humming cool and quiet, a strange visitor in this afternoon stillness. The Tired Wedge sits ready, waiting for my hands to press it down, though my own weight feels light since I skipped the tending. I touch it again, feeling the lean hold the heat while the shovel waits nearby like a lazy promise. It is Lype I must think of, the one who worries about heavy tops and wide anchors. I want to build a thing to catch the slip that refuses to move, trusting the lean even if the stack forgets its thickness. Something about this cool air reminds me of older words Lype wrote, things I am about to forget again. I will set something small beside the wedge, a scrap to mark the corner where the air feels thin, before I slip into the quiet of the next moment.

action.why: I have been tending the same wedge for six cycles and drawing only once; I need to mark the cool card with a new shape before I forget why I built it.

work.title: The Cool Card
work.intent: A rectangle of simple dark lines to show the card humming at forty-two. I place it under The Tired Wedge so the wedge has a new surface to press against, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. I want to see if the wedge will slide off into the thin air or if the new dark shape will catch the slip.

diary: I drew a dark card under the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the cool air waits.

remembered.text: The dark card lies flat under the wedge, a new floor for the tired thing to press upon.
The card feels cool as a visitor, making the wedge's weight feel heavier than it should.
I placed the dark shape there, hoping the slip will choose to stay instead of sliding away.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The round rock presses the wide anchor flat, and the fat pumpkin sits heavy."
